title: Loopy Farm: Idle Tycoon -> From web 2D game to 3D over one weekend
author: MrJurasek
selftext:
Last year I started working in my free time on my farming game dedicated for web and mobile.   
It is a cosy farming tycoon game where you get to drive your machines. You can plow, harvest, develop your farm and automate your production to improve your farm even further.   
Over 50 machines are available to collect.

It has been a great journey full of learnings. Since I started long ago when models were not on a level as they are today, I was carrying with myself a lot of technical complications and limitations.  
  
So at the end of October, over one Saturday evening, I gave Claude Code folder with my webgame files and started a small short experiment. Just to see how painful would it be, to move my game to Godot and make it from 2D to 3D. The result?

**Day 1** \- Ok, this might work!? World built in 3D, machines are already moving?  
**Day 3** \- All game features were completely moved to Godot  
**Days 4-7** \- Technical foundations (payments, cloud, performance optimisations for mobile etc.)  
**Day 7+** \- Internal Testing, New features, more polish, design iterations  
**Day 12** \- Game submitted to Google Play, waiting for the review. 

  
Cost of the development:   
**3D mobile** \- Everything done on Max subscription and I barely, BARELY hit the session limits.   
**OG 2D project** \- I was using Claude Pro (still available to play at [loopyfarm.com](https://loopyfarm.com/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=community&utm_campaign=r_aigamedev)  
Tech: **Godot + Opus 5.5**  
Music: **Gemini**  
Sounds: **Elevenlabs**, starter plan subscription  
Video made with: **Claude Code** \- runs scripts with various scenes directly in the game



Moving the game from web (react/pixijs) to Godot was best decision and it fixed me many legacy troubles that I was dealing with regularly. I should have done it much sooner.   
10/10 would recommend.
